summary: fsgg.managed-group-contract/1 is the supplier contract the Templates WASM caller binds at its Chromium support/runtime join (FS-GG/.github#4710 C-J1; Coordination issue https://github.com/FS-GG/FS.GG.Coordination/issues/1046, closed, under #1026). Pin (merged): FS-GG/FS.GG.Coordination commit ac22206560f3eddfea524ce8f752ff1d0dfeec4e (PR #1047, squash of independently reviewed head 317570839aad899dc3f0825f031cdd08efd1151e), path eng/managed_group_owner.py, sha256 d846dbe158befb5b824bd94a5bc0bb89b1145f825d5d6fa3a3225fa0451a36c0, 45315 bytes, one stdlib file. It is a sibling of eng/shared_process_owner.py, which contains by numeric process group and refuses detached groups/sessions; stock Playwright browser and Vite servers create such groups, and BCL Process sessions cannot observe re-parented descendants. Containment is a fresh leaf under an exclusive delegated cgroup v2 root; setsid/double-fork stays contained, and any process elsewhere in the root is an escape that fails the run. Birth is the unreaped child's pidfd plus start ticks and a /proc/<pid>/exe digest against profile leaderImages; the executable is hashed from an O_NOFOLLOW descriptor and exec'd through it; the leader gets no_new_privs, and an owner with effective uid 0 is refused (owner-privileged) because a recycled PID could then move or kill processes outside the root. Signals go through pidfds whose start ticks and cgroup are re-checked after opening. Retirement runs in separately guarded stages: SIGTERM, grace, leaf cgroup.kill, then a sweep of the whole delegated root (cgroup.kill of member-created cgroups at any depth, quarantine-and-kill for processes in the root or supervisor cgroup after a stable-birth check, owner relocation if moved), reap, drain to EOF, bottom-up removal. Late fix 1: the sweep items are guarded individually (relocate, census, residue, leaf state, leaf-kill, created-cgroup kills, quarantine create/move/kill, drain; the pidfd SIGKILL of members outside the root relies on the signal helper swallowing OSError) so one error is recorded as a sweep-<label> note and the sweep continues; a single error can no longer skip cgroup.kill. Late fix 2: an exiting task leaves cgroup.procs before it turns zombie, so absence from the root is no longer read as an escape; an escape now requires the same live, non-exiting birth (PF_EXITING clear, not zombie) whose own cgroup is outside the root. Cleanup is classified from a final root census (residualInRoot); custody is escaped-retired, escaped-unretired, unknown (residue without a recorded escape) or no-child; removal failure is reported, never hidden. Closed refusal codes precede launch. Lessons: independent review found that a single escape snapshot let fork-hopping, supervisor and nested escapees survive while the receipt claimed custody, that one drain error could skip cgroup.kill, all fixed with causal controls; a later hosted control run (job 119879840415) exposed a separate false-escape race for an exiting member, fixed in the merged source with a control. Leaf limits are cooperative because members share the owner's uid; hard limits and supervisor-death cleanup belong to the unit (sudo systemd-run, Delegate=yes, User=runner, NoNewPrivileges=yes, KillMode=control-group, TimeoutStopSec short, TasksMax/MemoryMax). A unit with NoNewPrivileges=yes masks the owner's prctl, so that control runs without it. The local dev container cannot delegate a cgroup and the owner refuses there. Hosted evidence on the reviewed head (required checks passed per the issue; hosted compiler-and-tests run 39799024069): 9 refusal-level and 21 containment controls, an owner-death control, and 25/25 single-fragment mutants killed. Known non-blocking review residuals recorded in the issue: no control for owner-privileged and probe() does not report it; no tests for owner relocation or for the escaped-unretired custody class, so those behaviours are implemented but not demonstrated by a control; an unreadable escapee cgroup fails open for privileged escapes only. Not established: hosted Templates runtime, browser support closure, the 27-case journey, publication or installed acceptance; this discharges only the process-group containment source portion of #1026. Supersedes the record citing unmerged revision 2bdfbc4c, whose pinned owner sha256 07053fd0... no longer names the merged file.
title: Managed-group candidate contract contains browser/process groups by delegated cgroup v2 with pidfd birth
